rationale.conceptual: The Gaspari-Gyorffy method and LAPW are established in computational condensed matter physics, but implementing the GG formula from the extracted electronic structure quantities (phase shifts, partial DOS, free-scatterer DOS) requires a solid grasp of the theory and meticulous post-processing. It is not a black-box call; genuine understanding of the equations is necessary.
rationale.execution: The reproduction involves multiple distinct stages: (1) crystal structure setup for two lattice constants, (2) self-consistent LAPW runs with dense k‑point grids, (3) extraction of DOS and phase shifts, (4) post‑processing to compute the GG formula. Requires using Elk, a specialised open‑source code, managing input files, convergence, and I/O between steps, making it a moderate pipeline.

The method is standard but non-trivial, involving multiple well-documented steps. The pipeline has several stages with dependencies and requires careful handling of a computational tool, making it moderately complex.
